utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, I'd just like to move on to another topic. In your examination-in-chief, you mentioned that you knew Zoran Krstevski. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You said that you remembered when he first started in the ministry and that you remember he started in September 2001. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right, somewhere towards the end of September 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And Zoran Krstevski was Minister Boskoski's advisor. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was senior advisor within the cabinet of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And he -- as senior advisor, Zoran Krstevski gave advice to the minister about important matters of the ministry. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't know what Mr. Krstevski advised the minister in regard with.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, wouldn't you expect that a senior advisor would give advice to the minister about important matters relating to perhaps current events in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the cabinet of the minister there are many jobs with the title advisor and they're divided into various areas. So the minister decides who is the advisor advising him on a specific matter. I don't really know what was the area that Mr. Krstevski was in charge of with regards to advising the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But, nevertheless, the reason he needed advisors was to assist him in his regular work as minister. Right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And may assist him in perhaps dealing with the press and current matters that the minister has to deal with on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of press you're speaking about, but surely he did help him in the everyday performance of the task with regards to the matters that the minister would request assistance in.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Dorevska, are you aware of the battle of Radusa which took place in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it was a battle between Macedonian forces and the Kosovo Protection members allegedly between -- in mid-August 2001. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer this question in the sense that you're asking me because my knowledge of that situation is that of any ordinary citizen of the state. The information that I received regarding that event primarily came from the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But you are aware that there was a battle in Radusa which engaged or involved the Macedonian security forces against allegedly hundreds of Kosovo protection members that crossed the border, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that some action took place in the village of Radusa, but who was battling against whom that is something beyond the domain of my work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you do know that the Macedonian security forces were involved in that action, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know they were involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to 65 ter 1160.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can have that, please, pulled up in the e-court. And also we do have some hard copy documents that we might distribute to Your Honours and to the witness at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, you see this is an article that is written by a journalist regarding the conflict of 2001. And you see that there's a picture on the very first page of that article, do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that is -- that's Zoran Krstevski. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is Zoran Krstevski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since we have the document on the screen, could our learned colleague help us and say when was this article written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may be possible. Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just in response to my friend's question, it appears to be written on the 28th of January, 2005, if I'm reading that correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, this article, Ms. Dorevska, deals with the battle at Radusa. And if I can just ask you to take a look at the second paragraph that begins with the phrase or the sentence: "Radusa also took place in 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you see how the next sentence after that says that: "The Macedonian security forces defending the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the state from the aggressors responded fiercely to the Albanian terrorists that infiltrated from the direction of Kosovo." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it continues to describe the battle between the Macedonian forces and the Albanians from -- from Kosovo and at the very end of that paragraph, it says: "We had the exclusive opportunity to hear how the operation in Radusa was conducted from a man who was in the team that led it, Zoran Krstevski." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then straight after that, it quotes Zoran Krstevski and he begins by saying: "The offensive started in the early hours of the morning, initially with a limited attack on the police station in Radusa." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then at about the middle of that paragraph he refers to the Ministry of Interior Tiger unit, and he says: "The Ministry of the Interior was immediately mobilised and the Tigers special tasks unit was sent to the area of Radusa without delay." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And at the very end or the bottom of that paragraph, the end of that long quote, it says: "Zoran Krstevski, the former senior advisor in the cabinet of former minister Ljube Boskoski." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I can't see that part on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It should be at the very bottom --

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is fine now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then there should be a heading that says headed -- in this article, titled: Luck for life. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the second paragraph underneath that heading says: "As the minister's advisor at that moment, I was required to be in the cabinet of the then prime minister Ljubco Georgievski so that I could monitor the development of events from there." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then at the -- then it continues to quote him as to what occurred. And if you look at the third page underneath the heading: Showdowns.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can perhaps ask that be shown on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it continues to quote Zoran Krstevski where he says: "There is no way that the encircled 30 or so police officers exposed to heavy attack could have caused so many casualties among the aggressor." And then he continues. Now, Ms. Dorevska, were you aware that Zoran Krstevski was working for the ministry at that time in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Zoran Krstevski started working for the ministry towards the end of September 2001, when he signed the contract with the Ministry of the Interior. I know that he came from the Macedonian Radio and television. I was already working then in the personnel department which means that I remember very well the time when Mr. Krstevski signed the employment contract.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, nevertheless, he may have signed the contract in September 2001, but doesn't this article clearly demonstrate that he was in fact working as the advisor to Minister Boskoski in 2001, in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This article, as you said, was written four years later by a person who was working in the media, in the Macedonian Television. I don't know why I should conclude that this is a reliable source of information.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, he was interviewed by a journalist regarding the battle in Radusa and he is quoted in the interview, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what is written here. But do you think that everything that is written in the media and everything that the individuals say must be accurate and reliable?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Don't you think, Ms. Dorevska, that if he was interviewed specifically in respect of the battle in Radusa and he provides all the details that he provides in this article that that indicates some reliability to the article?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't agree with your assessment. I can speak of the facts only, and the facts are stating something completely different, that during that time, Mr. Krstevski was not employed with the ministry and who could not hold the position discussed here. In the capacity of the employee in the minister, maybe he was an observer of the event as a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, he doesn't say that he was an observer of the event, does it? It says that he was in the cabinet of former minister Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't consider this a reliable evidence. If you believe that his statement is accurate and truthful and if you believe that this is evidence that should be taken into consideration, that's fine with you. But what I said I will repeat. This person, individual, has not been employed with the ministry during that time. He could not and he was not allowed to take any activities or make anything related to that job post.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was he assisting the ministry informally, even if he wasn't formally employed?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There shouldn't be any such situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Isn't it possible, Ms. Dorevska, that he was assisting the ministry informally, that Zoran Krstevski was assisting the ministry informally throughout this difficult and complex time that perhaps the formal procedures of employment were not followed?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that Minister Boskoski, for example, had sent telegrams because it was necessary to act most efficiently because of the complex situation in 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So at that complex time there may have been persons working with the ministry who were not officially employed with the minister perhaps like Zoran Krstevski, despite not having a formal contract. Isn't that possible?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not be possible and that would be illegal and such situation of course could not and must not take place.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it would be illegal for an individual to work for the ministry without a formal contract. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. From the moment one enters employment contract that is the moment from which there are obligations and duties of that person with regards to the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Would it be illegal for a person to assist the ministry without being an official employee?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it would be illegal. There are other formats of assistance. Maybe a contract, a task contract that would give the right to an individual to assist the ministry in that capacity. But in this case, there is no legal document indicating that the person had some duties to perform for the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you actually know for a -- personally, Ms. Dorevska, whether Zoran Krstevski was in fact assisting the ministry at that time?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What if minister -- what if Zoran Krstevski felt a moral obligation perhaps to assist the ministry given the events that were occurring at that time? Isn't it possible that he could assist the ministry and act as Minister Boskoski's advisor without a formal contract?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you think that just anyone who feels the moral obligation can come and assist the minister in carrying out his duties without entering a formal contract?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you. Isn't that possible?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I already answered this, that it is impossible and illegal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We've -- isn't it possible that given the complex situation in 2001 that there was some room for flexibility?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this part.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why was it legal, then, Ms. Dorevska, to have volunteers working for the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there were volunteers working for the ministry. There have been members of the reserve forces who worked for the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are volunteers reservists?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said reservists, not volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is it then possible for volunteers to become reservists?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, through a legal procedure, if they are recorded with the branch office of the Ministry of Defence and if through a procedure that applies to them, which is established in the Law on Defence and the Law on Internal Affairs become part of the reserve forces of the Ministry of the Interior, become reserve police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you account for the possibility, Ms. Dorevska, that the rules and regulations and the law may not address every possible situation that the police may encounter or that the minister may encounter, particularly in that complex time?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is always a way for the laws to be enforced, so to have the police conduct within the legal framework because the police conduct is always under public scrutiny, and every action outside of the competencies can be very delicate and could entail a very negative assessment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to another topic. Ms. Dorevska, yesterday we were looking at the Law on Internal Affairs, and you mentioned that the Law on Internal Affairs that was amended in 2003 formally gave the director independent powers. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did mention that in 2003 amendments were made to the Law on Internal Affairs, but they only confirmed the independence that the director had already have through the Law on Organisation and Work of the Bodies of Civil Service and the provisions of the rule book for organisation of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, you've already mentioned, however, that the rule book for the organisation of the ministry does not expressly refer to the independence of the director, does it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it establishes the bureau for public security as a body within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. If I can ask you to --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Or if I can perhaps ask that 65 ter 1158 be brought up in e-court. It's at tab 83 of the second Prosecution binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you see that on your screen, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that -- is that the law on amendment to the Law on Internal Affairs that was amended in 2003?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it specifically refers to, just to go through the document, under Article 1, new paragraph 2 is added which follows paragraph 1. And it says: "Organs within the structure of the ministry are the administration or the head of counter-intelligence and the bureau for the public security." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then underneath Article 7-a, we see the language that you had referred to earlier which specifically deals with the director for the bureau for public security. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I neglected to tender this yesterday and I'd like to tender it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: 65 ter 1158, the law on amendment in addition to the Law on Internal Affairs 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's just the 2003 amendment?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P571, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And while I'm at it, I'd like to also tender 65 ter 1159 -- 1155 at tab 29 which is the criminal charge brought by Goran Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P572, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd also like to tender 65 ter 1076, Ljube Boskoski's personnel file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P573, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, finally, I'd like to tender 65 ter 1160, the article that we just looked at relating to Zoran Krstevski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will not be objecting to the decision to the rulings, since you have already passed it down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be received as Exhibit P574, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. And, just for the record, I mentioned a document at tab 44 of the Prosecution binder. This is at transcript page 9544, and it should be Exhibit 1D211. If I may then continue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just moving on to another topic, Ms. Dorevska. You mentioned in your examination-in-chief that a code of conduct was circulated in 2001 to police. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were brochures, these were not a code of ethics.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why was it necessary to send -- to circulate brochures to members of the police?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why, because I did not take part in their preparation, publishing or distribution. I presume in order to assist the police officers in carrying out their daily activities and obligations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. You also said in your examination-in-chief that there were efforts being made to improve the ethnic structure in the ministry in 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that as of 2000, efforts were made to improve the ethnic structure but that at a given time this was halted. In September 2001, we continued to carry out these activities and we published an announcement for taking in 100 new police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But these efforts continued in 2001. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They continued, and also in the years that followed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And why did you need to recruit ethnic Albanians to improve the structure within the ministry, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say why because this is a normal thing for everyone and all communities to be represented in the ministry and in the state as a whole. This is part of the preamble of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Weren't there enough Albanians within the ministry at the time?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were very few, about four to five per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. You also mentioned at transcript page 9455 last week that there was no press information centre within the ministry in 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was no such organisational unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if there was no press centre at the time, who was writing all the public announcements to recruit members into the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the work of the sector which I head.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it was your sector that was drafting all the public announcements?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Public announcements for employment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, what if the minister had a press conference or needed information regarding a current event at that time, in 2001? How would he get that most up-to-date information in order to respond to the media?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Up to a period of time there was a person who was the spokesperson of the ministry who later left. After that I don't recall at all, and I don't think there was an official person who carried out this work. As to how this was done, I really could not tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was there an unofficial person who acted as spokesperson, perhaps, within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until May, or, rather, June 2001, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was there a spokesperson who acted on behalf of Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to move to another topic. Who -- before I do that, you mentioned, Ms. Dorevska, that it was your sector that drafted the public announcements to recruit members into the ministry. Who drafted the other kinds of public announcements?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know. Perhaps people from the minister's office, from the minister's cabinet who were in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And by that, you mean the minister's advisors.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Most probably some of the advisors of the minister. If you believe that there was someone charged to that end, or for this task.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just moving then on to another topic. At transcript page 9497, Ms. Dorevska, you said that any superior officer could initiate a disciplinary procedure against an employee from within his subordination. And you said that the proposal could be filed by the director of the bureau for public security and for the state security and the officers who are authorised by the minister. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So let me see if I understand what you're saying. If a police officer in Mirkovci police station, for example, commits an act of misconduct or even a criminal act, can the deputy commander for Mirkovci file a proposal for disciplinary proceedings against him?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He cannot file a proposal for initiating a disciplinary proceeding because the contract for transfer authorisation lists the person who can do this. But this which you raised as an issue the deputy commander can initiate this to the person who is authorised to file the proposal and this is the head of the section who will then convey this to the sector of internal affairs, because he is the person authorised with a decision to file such proposals.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Let me just see if I understand what you're saying. The deputy commander of the police station can inform the head of the section, or the head commander, and, in turn, the head of the police station, of Mirkovci for example, would inform the head of the SVR, the sector, and it is the head of the sector that files a proposal. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. When there's an initiative of the kind that we're speaking about now and there is evidence and statements in written form, they are compiled and are submitted up the chain of command to the person authorised to file that proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Wouldn't the immediate superior also be authorised to file a proposal, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All direct superiors are not authorised. Only those persons who are listed in the decision passed by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So the minister can decide who he wishes to authorise and who he wishes not to authorise to file -- to initiate disciplinary proceedings. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will quote the provision from the collective agreement which clearly states a proposal for initiating or carrying out disciplinary proceeding can be submitted by the director. It's listed as under-secretary there because of the older date of the collective agreement or other persons authorised by the minister, which means that the minister is obliged to reach such a decision and to decide who he will pass on this authority to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, what if the head of the sector fails to initiate a proceeding against the police officer in Mirkovci police station, can then the head of the uniformed police or the head of the crime police initiate that proceeding?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean if he does not initiate this, whether that other person would undertake this obligation? This should not be the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can the head of the uniformed police or the crime police initiate proceedings against the head of the sector for failing to initiate the disciplinary proceeding?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can, because he is authorised by the decision -- by a decision to file such a proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So if the head of the uniformed police or the crime police is authorised by decision to file a proposal, why can't he initiate a proceeding against the police officer in Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the decision for transfer of authorisation, you can see that it lists the persons who are authorised and persons against whom proposals can be submitted in a disciplinary proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Doesn't that proposal list the persons who are authorised to initiate disciplinary proceedings in general?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, it lists also against whom these proposals may be submitted. Specifically, it lists that the director of the bureau for public security can file a proposal for disciplinary proceeding against employees in the ministry which means that the director of public security is obliged to file a proposal for my work post, which is under the direct supervision of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can the director of the public security initiate proceedings against the head of the uniformed police, for example?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. This is possible, to initiate and to file a proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can the head -- can the director of the bureau of public security initiate a proceeding against the head of a sector?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is possible. They can initiate a proceeding and they can file a proposal against a head of sector. In principle, initiatives come from the ground, from the direct superiors and those who will assess that a certain person has overstepped his or her authorisations or by the sector of internal control which in fact is in charge of looking over such conduct or misconduct by employees. In any rate, there is a difference between an initiative and a proposal for a disciplinary proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What I understand you to be saying is that the director of the public bureau for security can initiate a proceeding. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there -- there is knowledge received from the head of an organisational unit, then he can initiate such a proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can the head of the -- director of the bureau of public security initiate a proceeding against the head of the OVR?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can initiate and point to the authorised person for filing such a proceeding, and this is the head of sector that there are informations to that end received, for example, from the sector of internal control and that a proceeding should be taken against such a person.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So he can instruct the head of sector to initiate a proceeding against the head of the OVR. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe that you're not making the distinction between an initiative and a proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, my question is: Can the director of bureau of public security bring a proposal against the head of the OVR?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, no, because the head of the sector of internal affairs is already authorised by a decision of the minister to submit proposals. The director can give the initiative on the basis of certain knowledge which he has received so that the head of sector can officially submit this proposal because he is the authorised person to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But what if the head of the sector who is one of the authorised persons to bring the proposal fails to bring that proposal? Can't the director of bureau of public security then bring a proposal against the head of the OVR?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, the head of sector will be punished for this and he will establish the reasons why he had not done what he should have done and if this is not done then the director can also submit a proposal if we have a serious situation at hand, which must be acted upon, and for which there's a danger of statute of limitations and deadlines.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And who would the head of sector be punished? By whom would the head of sector be punished if he does -- if he fails to initiate or submit a proposal?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can be sanctioned by the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So the director can initiate then or bring the proposal against the head of the sector for failing in that regard. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. However, there is also another sanction provided for by Article 75 or 76 of the collective agreement, which means the sanction can be 15 per cent of his salary, the reasoning being that he failed to undertake necessary measures which is different than the disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm just asking you about the disciplinary proceedings for the time being. Now, you mentioned earlier that -- that the initiative comes from the ground. You said that the initiative to -- or the report, if I understand what you're saying, regarding the disciplinary or the act of misconduct that goes to the director comes from the ground. Now, what if that initiative does not come from the ground? What if it comes from somewhere else? Then at that stage can the director initiate or bring the proposal against a police officer in a police station?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The director can obtain such information. But, once again, he will inform the head and the authorised person for submitting such a proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can the assistant to the sector bring a proposal against a police officer in, say, for example, Mirkovci or Karpos police station?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unless he is expressly authorised by the minister with a decision to do so, then he cannot. He can only submit an initiative.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So isn't it possible, then, Ms. Dorevska, that the -- that the minister can authorise virtually anybody to -- to bring a proposal for disciplinary proceedings? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I quoted the provision of the collective agreement. Or persons authorised by the minister. And I believe that lawyers will interpret this as it is written.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So is your answer to my question yes, that he can authorise virtually anybody in the ministry to initiate a proceeding?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister decides who he will authorise. He may authorise only the directors, or the employees who are in management positions but are subordinate to the directors. These are authorised officials from higher organisational units of in charge of the units which they are in charge of, because of the overall structure of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But I take it your answer, then, is that the minister can authorise any worker or employee within the ministry to initiate a disciplinary proceeding. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to initiate. To file a proposal, to bring a proposal for a disciplinary proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when one files a proposal or brings a proposal for a disciplinary proceeding, isn't that the start of the disciplinary proceeding? Isn't that what begins the process? Isn't that at point go to the commission for the procedures to commence?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the moment when the proposal is drafted in written form with all elements listed in the collective agreement, the person authorised to sign and file this proposal submits this to the commission also set up by a decision of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you said, Ms. Dorevska, that the minister cannot initiate proceedings. That was your testimony, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the minister cannot submit a proposal for a disciplinary proceeding because is he not expressly authorised to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Where does it say in the collective agreement or in any other law that the minister cannot submit a proposal for disciplinary proceeding?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Provision in the collective agreement is very clear. If the minister has the authorisation to file a proposal, then the provision will be different and will say a proposal for the disciplinary proceeding can be submitted by a minister, director, or other so authorised persons. In this case, there's no such provision. Therefore, no authorisation for the minister. There's also the Law on Civil Servants, regulating the civil service in general and in the ministry there are also persons with the status of civil servants. In this law you will also find a provision which states that the direct superior submits a proposal for disciplinary proceeding. No minister in the country is not authorised to file proposals for disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is the minister authorised to initiate a disciplinary proceeding, can he advise the director for the bureau of public security to initiate a disciplinary proceeding, for example?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he has information that misconduct has been committed, something not in accordance someone's obligation then the minister can of course point out to the director or ask the director whether this is so and whether measures need to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, suppose the minister had information that there were police members or police officers within the ministry that committed an act of misconduct or criminal activity, could the minister have directed the director for the bureau of public security to file a proposal for disciplinary proceeding?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He cannot direct him. He can speak with them, they can speak about this particular topic so the director can undertake the obligations which are his, to investigate the case, to see whether conditions for such a proceeding and to take the necessary measures to that end.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, what if the director disagrees with the minister and refuses or fails to file a proposal for -- to initiate a disciplinary proceeding? Can the minister not instruct him at that point to do so?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because, most probably, in such a case the director has assessed that there are no conditions for carrying out a disciplinary proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But what if the minister disagrees with the director and thinks the director is wrong in his assessment that -- that there were no conditions to carry out a disciplinary measure? Can the minister at that point instruct the director to initiate a disciplinary proceeding?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because the minister cannot have knowledge to that extent, whether their conditions for the disciplinary proceedings are in place or not. In a way, this is a court proceeding, a short court proceedings with its own rules. Not any person on the basis of wishes or knowledge can independently or self-willingly initiate such a proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, suppose the minister happened to witness an act of misconduct or criminal activity and he therefore does have the knowledge, can he then at that stage instruct the director, or anybody else, to initiate a disciplinary proceeding?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot think about all of these situations which you are mentioning. Maybe you're speaking about a police officer working on a cross-road and when the minister is passing and then when the minister passed, he saw that he was not properly uniformed. I don't know the situation you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, let's suppose the minister was passing and he was at a police station and he saw that a police officer was -- was beating up a civilian.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that something of this kind cannot happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Let's assume that it has happened, Ms. Dorevska. Let's just assume for a moment that the minister saw that police officer was beating up a civilian. Can he not at that point instruct the director to initiate a disciplinary proceeding?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If he went to the police station, as you say, let us presume he saw police officers beating civilian, he would turn to the chief to undertake certain measures towards the police officer who is beating the civilian and to see what is at hand.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So he would instruct the chief to initiate a disciplinary proceeding against the police officer who beat the civilian. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You say that he could be a witness to this. I'm telling that you this situation cannot happen, but since these are all presumptions, all superiors control the work of his subordinates, which means that the superior is the person who initiates the proceeding. Perhaps the minister could initiate a proceeding for me, and to tell the person who is authorised to file proposals that I have had an act of misconduct on the best of his knowledge, but against those persons who are in work posts under the direct authorisation of the minister, a disciplinary proceeding against them is submitted by the director of public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Suppose the minister saw on the TV on the news, on the TV news, that there were acts of misconduct by police officers such as the beating of civilians. Isn't it possible for then the minister to instruct the director to initiate proceedings against those police officers?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In that case it would not be possible but there are other measures that he could take that are within the area of his competence. He could address the head of internal control and ask them to examine the case. He could establish a committee that would then work on clarifying the case to arrive at final information that could then lead to disciplinary procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And suppose the minister set up a commission to investigate, say, alleged criminal activity, by police members or acts of misconduct, can he then instruct members of the commission, depending on their findings, to initiate disciplinary proceedings or even submit a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he establishes a committee that needs to do it, then the committee needs to submit its opinion on the basis of the activities and actually analysis of the situation and the conclusions drawn on the basis of the entire procedure, and usually that opinion is submitted to the minister. The minister being the person who authorised the committee. If the committee establishes that there has been abuse of office, then, or misconduct, then this case will be forwarded to the person who is responsible for initiating a disciplinary procedure. While if it has been established that no misconduct was found, then no further measures will be taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can the minister instruct members of the committee to recommend the instigation of proceedings, should they find that there were acts of misconduct that had taken place?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The committee will be independent in the performance of its duties and once the minister has established it, he has given his full consent to the committee undertaking any activity necessary. And if the committee makes the assessment that there has been misconduct, then further measures will be taken and the procedure will be instigated as prescribed by the collective agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can the minister initiate further measures, should there be -- should the committee, for example, find that there were acts of misconduct, of criminal activity perpetrated by members of the ministry, or police officers?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could not suggest undertaking any further measures if it has been found that misconduct or criminal offence has taken place because these are two different procedures. Then, the measures will be undertaken by the persons who are authorised to undertake such measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why can't the minister suggest the undertaking of further measures in those circumstances, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What would be the further measures? The proposal for the disciplinary measures is the start of the procedure. Any evidence and everything else is established through the procedure. The minister does not have any suggestions to make or guidelines to give with regards to a procedure that hadn't started yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can the minister, for example, instruct or advise members of the committee to submit criminal charges, should they find that criminal activity had taken place by police members?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the committee makes the assessment that it would be founded to establish a criminal -- to instigate a criminal procedure, then it will be taken to the sector for internal affairs or to the unit where the person works and advise the instigation of criminal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you suggesting, Ms. Dorevska, that the minister has no authority to follow up on the findings of a commission or a committee that he created?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're saying, just to be clear for the record, that no, he has no authority to follow up on the findings of a commission or a committee that he created. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The committee will forward it to the services in charge of the further course of the procedure, if there is a ground to instigate any procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what if the committee fails to do that? The minister can do nothing?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you think that the minister will phone the competent services and forward their report? There are procedures that are followed in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, if you still have your first binder, I'd like you to please turn to tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please call up 1D113 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Have you found tab 15, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tab 15, rules amending the rules on organisation and operation of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, that's the wrong tab. Perhaps what I can do is ask you -- I think you have the wrong binder. If I can ask you to look on your screen.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the screen, I see it, the decision to establish a committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So you see there that this is a resolution or decision by Minister Boskoski for the formation of a commission to investigate the validity of the reports by ethnic Albanians in the Republic of Macedonia that members of the Ministry of Interior violated their authority. Do you see that? I'd just like you to please look at the first page.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the commission is formed and there's number of names there. And we see that on the first page, under paragraph II it says that: "The commission outlined in part 1 of this resolution is assigned the task of determining the validity of the allegations contained in the reports, both individual and group, which were submitted to the Ministry by ethnic Albanian citizens of the Republic of Macedonia claiming that certain members of the ministry violated their authority during the completion of their work." Do you see that? Do you see -- I'm asking to you look at the first page, please. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is in the second page in my binder. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And then it says: "The commission is to immediately act on the tasks established in part II of this resolution and to investigate all reports received thus far and that will be submitted to the Ministry of Interior in the future." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if you look at paragraph V of the -- of this document, it says that the commission outlined in part one of this resolution will dispatch an answer to the submitter of the report and will inform the minister of interior and other competent organs of its findings and recommendations for every individual report." Then it goes on and it says, if you look at the last paragraph: "If the commission finds that certain members of the Ministry of Interior violated their authority, it will recommend the instigation of procedures to determine the degree of responsibility due to violation of work discipline by the competent organs of the ministry or the submission of criminal charges to the public prosecutor ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So here we have a decision by the minister, Ms. Dorevska, where he is instructing, he is telling the commission that if they find that members of the ministry violated their authority, or violated the work discipline, that it will recommend the instigation of proceedings, disciplinary procedures or the submission of criminal charges. Right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the content of the decision. The minister has the right to issue such decisions. This is a customary practice in the ministry, and he is authorised for this, pursuant to the rule book, and of course these decisions are prepared by the sector where I work, and its contents should present detailed description of the competencies of the committee. This is just stating that the committee should assess whether there is abuse of powers and propose that the procedures instigated to establish the responsibility, if the conditions for this are met. This is not guideline given by the minister. The minister, when signing the decision, has authorised the committee to undertake those activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, hasn't the minister gone a step further and actually instructed members of the committee that they will recommend the instigation of procedures in the event that a violation of duty has been found. Isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document just provides authorisation to the committee to investigate certain situation and certain case and if it makes its assessment that there has been misconduct, to continue the procedure within the legally prescribed elements.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Doesn't the committee have to also follow the instruction to instigate proceedings or submit a criminal charge in the event that they find that there was a violation of duty by members of the ministry? Isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this committee, when working, makes the assessment that there are grounds for that, it will inform the director of public or of state security depending on the activities at hand, and the officers in charge of that will undertake the activities, will make a proposal or will, if appropriate, file a criminal report with the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you, Ms. Dorevska. I asked you that this decision expressly states by the minister to the committee that it will instigate proceedings or submit criminal charges, should a violation of duty be found. Doesn't it? It's a simple question that requires a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not like that. I believe that what you are reading does not correspond to the situation indicated in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you suggesting, then, that the paragraph doesn't say that if the commission finds that certain members of the ministry violated their authority, it will recommend the instigation of proceedings or submit criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What you stated now, the committee will complete its work and will recommend, make a recommendation to those who are authorised to continue the procedure further. I believe that the wording is very clear indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It also says that -- it also says that or the submission of criminal charges to the public prosecutor. And this is based on the instructions of the minister, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the instructions of the minister. There is a difference between a criminal offence and violation of the working discipline. The both possibilities are indicated here. The persons could have perpetrated a criminal offence for which they would have been held responsible in a criminal procedure, actually criminal procedure would have been instigated, whereas if there was no criminal offence but only violation of the working discipline, then a procedure will be instigated to establish their responsibility because of the violation of the working discipline.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, you haven't answered my question. My question was: This instigation -- or the requirement for the committee, this sentence where it says that the committee will recommend the instigation of procedures or submit criminal charges is based on the instruction of the minister. Right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the competencies of the committee, authorisations given by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But isn't the minister instructing the committee to recommend the instigation of proceedings or submit criminal charges? Isn't that what he is doing?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not give an instruction. This is just the contents of the decision. If, a decision like this is made, in itself it must contain certain elements, it must contain guidelines as to what this committee needs to do. These are simply the tasks for the committee. It is not possible that the decision contains only the names of the individuals without giving the tasks that these individuals are to perform.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So is the minister tasking the committee, then, to instigate disciplinary proceedings or submit criminal charges in the event that a violation is found?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I repeated several times, that this committee has just the obligation to establish whether there was abuse of powers, misconduct. It is not instigating the procedure. The procedure will be instigated by those who are authorised for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, are you suggesting that every committee that -- that is charged with gathering evidence or investigating a criminal activity refers to -- has this reference in -- in that decision, that it must recommend the instigation of proceedings, disciplinary proceedings or submit criminal charges?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is given as a task for the committee, in the decision itself, then surely the committee is authorised to recommend that the next committees or bodies undertake the activities for which they are authorised. This is not a disciplinary committee. This is a committee established by a minister's decision to investigate whether there has been any misconduct or abuse of powers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You still haven't answered my question, though, Ms. Dorevska. My question is: The minister, in this case, had specifically given this task to this committee to instigate disciplinary proceedings or submit criminal charges in the event that a violation of duty was found. Right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, I've -- I must confess that I have difficulty reading Article 5 in the way that you do. It seems to me that the word "recommend" qualifies the two alternative positions that follow, both the procedures for -- the instigation of procedures in the work discipline situation, or the submission of criminal charges.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, my focus, Your Honour was on the word -- the term or the word "will."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: "Will recommend" is what I focus on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Which I'm suggesting is an instruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's an instruction to recommend.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Both in respect of procedures in the work discipline context and the submission of criminal charges. You seem to be putting to the witness that it was a recommendation in the first of those two cases but a direction to actually submit criminal charges in the second, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I see Your Honour's point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your thread of cross-examination, though, would still be there: What happens if the committee does not make a recommendation, is the minister in a position to do anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, perhaps just picking up on His Honour's question, if in the event that the committee finds a violation of duty but does not recommend the instigation of proceedings or the submission of criminal charges, is the minister in a position at that point to take action or instruct the director, for example, for the bureau of public security to take action against those members that violated their duty?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No such situation could occur. The committee was given a specific task. It needs to submit a report to the minister as it is written in paragraph IV. If it is written in this report that the individuals have abused their powers as the committee has established, then the committee has the duty to forward the report for further processing. I don't know whether or why you believe that the committee can find that there have been abuses and this ends the procedure. It has never happened in the practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take note of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now and resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, you have told us that the minister does not make the ultimate decision on the issue of punishment after the commission has made its proposal to the minister, and that is because there is a right of appeal, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister reaches the decision after the proposal has been submitted by the disciplinary commission, or committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And he reaches that decision -- he can actually change the decision or the proposal that was submitted by the commission. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right. There is such provision in the collective agreement, which gives such right to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And should someone decide not to appeal, then the minister's decision effectively becomes the last one made, or the final decision, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in some cases, the appeals commission may simply agree with the minister's decision, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the appeals commission makes its decision on the basis of the record from the disciplinary hearing, together with the minister's decision. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The second instance commission at the government collects all materials which are related to the case and on the basis of this, reaches its decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And apart from the -- from the process of appeal, the minister is the final decision-maker as prescribed in Article 149 of the collective agreement, right, within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The minister is authorised to reach the decision by which a measure of sanction is stated after the end of the disciplinary proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if an employee commits a crime, or criminal charges are referred to public prosecutor against him, he can still undergo disciplinary proceedings at the same time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just moving on to another topic. Ms. Dorevska, you were talking about reservists. And to clarify one point, you said that if a reservist did not follow the orders of the active officer which he is subordinated to, then the head or commander of the police station will inform the competent organisational unit. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember having said this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now just to clarify, what do you mean when you say that the commander of the police station will inform the competent organisational unit?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're now talking about reservists. In such a case, he will inform the regional unit of the Ministry of Defence where this person is registered and is on the list of reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And he will inform the regional unit of the Ministry of Defence that the person should be disengaged or should be removed from the list of reservists for committing a violation or refusing an order?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reasons are enumerated by the head. I would like to clarify, however, that this is not my scope of work and I can only speak about what is listed in the law. In my long-term experience in the ministry have led me to some of these procedures which are implemented by people who are in the unit for defence preparations who are in charge of reservists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I add, Ms. Issa, that as I understood the evidence, the effect of the reporting procedure indicated by Ms. Dorevska is that the reservists' name may be taken off the roll of reservists in the ministry of interior, not that he would cease to be [Realtime transcript read in error "not that be would be"] a reservist subject to the control of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I was actually just getting to that point where I was going to clarify that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just to clarify that point, Ms. Dorevska, once a reservist fails to follow an order or commits a violation, then, as His Honour has mentioned, the reservist's name is then removed from the roll of the reservists from the Ministry of Interior and then becomes disengaged. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is a case of a smaller infringement, failure to respect work of obligations he is charged with, then this is the procedure which is implemented and this person is struck from the roll of the ministry with information to the Ministry of Defence to that end. However, if we have a criminal act, then the authorised persons can then undertake a misdemeanour or criminal procedure against this person.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. I put to it to you, Ms. Dorevska, that the rules and the law of internal affairs and the other rules and laws that you've described, particularly the Law on Internal Affairs, demonstrate that in 2001, that the ministry of interior was a centralised structure with a strict hierarchy with the minister at the top of that hierarchy. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in full. There is a hierarchy. There is one now, however, the organisational units have certain independence in their activities and the -- and the bodies within have the independence as provided by the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I put it to you that in 2001, Minister Boskoski had oversight and control over members of the ministry, including the police as demonstrated by the various orders and decisions he made. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he had oversight over the work of the ministry and of course he must also have control, but I don't know the context in which you are saying this. The minister is the person who represents the ministry and is obliged to look into the state of affairs of the ministry of which is he in charge.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I put it to you, Ms. Dorevska, that Minister Boskoski did not follow the black letter law and was in control over police units and police operations within the ministry in 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I put it to you, Ms. Dorevska, that during that complex time in 2001, that as Minister Boskoski said in his book, he liked to keep his hands into everything and that he saw himself as a great liberator of Macedonia. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Of course, he had all necessary information he needed to manage and to lead the ministry in a proper and conscientious manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Issa. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good evening, Madam Dorevska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you commence, Ms. Residovic, could I just mention that page 38, line 16, what I said should be recorded "not that he would cease to be a reservist subject to the control of the Ministry of Defence." "Cease to" has been omitted in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good evening, Ms. Dorevska.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good evening to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will start by putting questions that follow up on the questions my learned friend put last and I will go back to some of the answers you gave to these questions today. Do you recall, Madam Dorevska, of -- or rather, that my learned friend from the OTP asked you whether it was true that the minister could authorise individuals to file applications for disciplinary proceedings and that on several occasions you quoted the relevant provision of the collective agreement whereby the ministry is given that authorisation. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you also recall that my colleague put it to you that the minister could authorise any individual with the right to instigate disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown 1D275, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Dorevska, I'm sorry that we don't have the hard copies of the decision, but we can see that it was adopted on the 8th of November, 1999. Do you know what this document is all about?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision what the minister has as an obligation from the collective agreement to authorise person who can start a proceeding for disciplinary procedure and to remove -- removal from a work post as a result of this proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Dorevska, do you recognise in this decision the relevant organs that the minister authorised to issue such a proposal for the institution of disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the persons -- or, rather, the work posts of these persons that are authorised to submit such a proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please turn to page 2 of the document. Madam Dorevska, can you tell which minister it was who issued the stated decision back in 1999?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Mr. Pavle Trajanov.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown Exhibit 1D276 now, please. This decision was issued on the 20th of September, 2005. Madam Dorevska, do you recognise the document before you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document prepared in the sector which I head.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please turn to the following page of the document. Madam Dorevska, please look at item III -- no, II, starting: "The entering into form of this decision."

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. This means that with this decision the validity of the decision we spoke about earlier ceases to be valid.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the period between 1990, when Minister Pavle Trajanov issued the decision designating the posts authorised to issue a proposal for the institution of disciplinary proceedings and 2005, when this decision was issued, can you tell me which persons holding which posts or positions were in fact authorised to issue such proposals?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those listed in the decision adopted in 1999 by Mr. Pavle Trajanov.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, yesterday you were asked this question and I'll repeat it today. Is it possible, and is it a frequent practice, whereby a staffing table or a systematic decision is -- remains in force although the ministers change?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course this happens in practice unless there is a charge of organisational or other reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001 and 2002, if I may be so bold as to draw the following conclusion on the basis of what you said, the authorised bodies or rather the persons holding relevant posts allowing them to ask for the institution of the disciplinary proceedings were in fact the persons that were listed back in that decision dating from 1999. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with the disciplinary procedure, Madam Dorevska, do you recall my learned friend asking you about who was supposed to initiate and who was supposed to launch disciplinary proceedings and what would happen if the individual charged with instituting the proceedings fails to do so? Do you recall discussing this matter with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall being asked the question, whether the chief of the OVR Cair or any other OVR, or whether if he himself failed to initiate disciplinary proceedings whether the proceedings could be initiated by the head of the bureau for public security instead? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what is the deadline within which a disciplinary procedure has to be instituted?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be instigated within a period of three months. This is a subjective deadline, from the day when one learns, or an objective deadline of six months from the day that act was committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If a disciplinary offence occurred in August of 2001, what would be the latest possible deadline by which a disciplinary proceeding ought to be instituted?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until six months from the day that that act was committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If beyond that deadline any individual who is authorised with instituting a disciplinary proceeding, be it head of the sector or the head of the bureau for public security, that particular individual learned that the person who was supposed to institute disciplinary proceedings failed to do so, would the authorised individual, head of the sector or the head of the bureau, be able to institute such proceedings beyond the deadline, after it has expired?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, once this deadline is overstepped then is there is a statute of limitation and this cannot -- and a disciplinary proceeding cannot be initiated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If in the summer of 2002 the head of the bureau for public security learned from the relevant employees about a head of one of the departments of the interior refusing to take part in clearing up certain events, was that particular individual, the head of that body, able to do anything to take any measures to launch disciplinary proceedings at that point?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could not undertake anything with respect to disciplinary proceeding at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I don't really see how this line of questioning arises from the cross-examination. It seems to me that these are matters that Ms. Residovic could have raised in her examination-in-chief. I certainly didn't ask any questions in relation to the deadlines of when proceedings can be commenced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you've finished with this topic any way, haven't you, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
