utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did in fact. But the question didn't have to do with the statute of limitations at all. It was merely the case of when a director would be able to institute disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me - this was something that was already discussed - if a minister were to set up a commission tasked with shedding light on certain events, which measures could be taken once the commission has completed its work? We've had a number of questions on that matter. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, tell me, if the commission in question, or the relevant body, having examined the events, still fails to establish the facts that would be relevant for a conclusion that a person has committed an official misconduct or a crime or a criminal offence, would it be possible to take any other measures within the disciplinary procedure?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not. If the commission had finished its work and submitted a report stating there is no overstepping of authorisation, there is no possibility to undertake or initiate a proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Dorevska, if one were to presume that, nevertheless, a member of the police force did overstep his authority, there being reason to suspect that someone overstepped their authority, but without in fact being able to identify the perpetrator involved, would it be possible for the competent body which should propose disciplinary proceedings to in fact get involved in such a procedure without knowing the perpetrator involved?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Unlike the criminal proceeding, the disciplinary proceeding cannot be led against an unknown person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend asked you the following: Whether the reserve force can be subject to disciplinary proceedings and my learned friend referred you to your statement where you stated that it was impossible. She asked you what were the steps taken by the commander of the police station and you answered that. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour. Before the witness responds if I may make an objection, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think it's slight misrepresentation. It is incorrect to say that I asked the witness about the -- whether reserve forces can be subject to disciplinary proceedings. That wasn't what I asked the witness. I simply asked the witness to clarify one matter that she testified about in her examination-in-chief and that is what she had said about the head -- whether -- how the information gets to the head commander. And then after the head commander becomes aware of an overstepping of a -- of the bounds what -- what happens at that stage. But I don't think that I asked -- I asked the question in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on, please, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, although this is not within your direct competences, but you stated that your experience from within the police gives you the opportunity to provide some answers. Tell me whether this procedure was applicable in 2001 and 2002 as well?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was in force.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend asked you several questions pertaining to the position of the advisor to the minister, Mr. Zoran Krstevski. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask that the witness is shown again 65 ter 1160. It has now some exhibit number, but I'm not sure which one is it. Do you see the text in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that my learned colleague read from the first column, some of the text which says: "During the almost four years the public was continuously hearing a version that it needed to hear, because at that time it suited somebody for it to be that way." Do you recall that this paragraph was read out to you by my learned friend?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, this is now Exhibit P574. Answering that question, I will quote liberally. You stated that you could not see how you would consider reliable an article written in some newspaper four years later. Do you remember that you gave an answer to this extent?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my answer, the extent of my answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This text that was shown to you by my learned friend stating that in the most recent four years, the public has continuously heard the version that was supposed to be heard. In your opinion, does it corroborate your testimony before this Court, that it would be difficult to believe what is stated or what is rumoured in the public in this --

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I hold by what I have said. I really cannot believe texts published in newspapers as reliable sources for a situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, considering that your narrow field of speciality is employment and labour, you are for years already head of that department, would it be possible for a person to simultaneously have full employment status in several organisations or bodies?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not possible. Only in one body, one organ.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask now that the Exhibit 1D285 is shown. When asked by my learned friend you stated that you remembered very well when Mr. Zoran Krstevski became an employee with the Ministry of the Interior because during that time, you worked there. Tell me, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the contract of employment by -- concluded between Mr. Zoran Krstevski and the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of this contract, it is stated that the collective agreement applies from the 27th of September, 2001. Does this text of the agreement agree, does it corroborate what you stated that his employment started towards September 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is confirms this and this is the date as of which Mr. Krstevski, like all other employees, are registered in the employment bureau as an employed individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask that the witness is shown 65 ter 1D1278.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters kindly ask the counsel to move the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You recall, Ms. Dorevska, that you answered one of the questions in stating that you were aware that Mr. Zoran Krstevski was previously an employee of the Macedonian Television.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew that he worked in the Macedonian Television, because we had the opportunity to watch him on our TV screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have a document in front of you that the Defence received from the Prosecutor's office from the 25th of September, 2001, and this is an application or request from Zoran Krstevski, advisor to the director general of the Macedonian Radio and Television requesting for termination of working relations with the Macedonian Radio and Television because of the transfer to a new job. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, does this document corroborate, as well, your testimony before this Court that until this date Zoran Krstevski was the employee of the Macedonian Radio and Television?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see the date, the 24th of September, 2001. This is the day prior to his work in the ministry, which means that his previous employment had to end, that he had to terminate this or register this at the agency for employment, and then to start his employment at the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to go back to some of the issues that my learned friend asked you yesterday. Do you remember that towards the end of yesterday's evidence you discussed with my learned friend the issue of the minister, the issue of Mr. Boskoski, having not received the decision requesting that he return some award, some pistol. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you recall that you then stated that every citizen can refuse to receive the decision, but that the legal system has resolved the issue of proper service in a situation when somebody refuses to voluntarily receive a decision. Is that so? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, with regards to certain rights and obligations entailed in a decision, when do they start to apply?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They can start to apply when the decision is properly served or another document in question is served.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does it mean, rights and obligations? What right is then earned by the person to which this document or a decision is served?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When a person receives a decision in any of the ways that we spoke about now, this person has now the right to raise an objection before the relevant commission in the government or to file a complaint with the relevant court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And until it is decided upon the appeal, or complaint of the person to whom the decision was served, do the obligations from that decision have any standing, especially are they in legal force, with regards to the person who is the recipient of the decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not. The appeal delays the execution of the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that the person could appeal or instigate a civil law procedure, if they believed that decision unlawfully violates their rights. Is that what you stated just now? Have I understood you well?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. A procedure can be raised between the competent courts for him or her to realise his rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know -- I apologise. First of all, you stated answering the questions of my learned friend yesterday, that the award was bestowed in accordance with the regulations or rules of the Ministry of the Interior. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that question, whether the award was bestowed lawfully or not, was it ever raised before a competent court?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course in the sector where I work, because we work in areas of representation before the courts, there are many such cases, similar cases before the courts, but the courts have not yet made their decisions whether these decisions are lawful or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We would move to another question, Ms. Dorevska. Answering yesterday questions asked by my learned friend the Prosecutor, you mentioned the Article 55 of the Law on Organisation and Operation of the Bodies of Civil Service several times, and you enumerated the competencies that any minister has, also orders, but you stressed that this applies if the minister is authorised by the law. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, could the minister vest in himself competences that do not belong to him under the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When this provision of the law states, if authorised by law, could you tell us which is the law referred to here?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the laws that we mentioned. The Law on Organisation and Work of the State Administration Bodies, the Law on Government, the Law on Internal Affairs and also in some other laws mentioned at the onset of my testimony which pertain to matters of internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering some previous questions, if I understood well, you further elucidated your position with regards to this and you stated that the legal basis for the decision of the minister could be the law, a government's decision or a decision of the president. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to indicate page 9540 and 9541, pages of the transcript, particularly -- 9450 and 9451.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why do you believe, Ms. Dorevska, that the decision or a conclusion of the government would be mandatory, would put the minister under obligation?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the government is a collective body and because the minister is responsible for his work before the government. The government passes decisions which are obligatory and mandatory for the ministries.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, in your second binder, could you find this exhibit, P -- this is in tab 40. This is Prosecutor's Exhibit P551. This would be in the Prosecutor's binder. It is after tab 40. And I would kindly ask you to look at the Article 36 of the law. That is in page N000-2531; that is the Macedonian page. Unfortunately, I don't have the English version in my binder here. That is Article 36. And I would kindly ask you to read now Article 36, item 3, which says: "By its decision the government decides on certain issues and the measures related to enforcement of the law, establishes professional and other services or bodies for its purposes and joined services, bodies to serve the needs of the ministries and other bodies of the civil service." Does this provision of the Law on Government authorises the government to decide about the methods of enforcement of all laws, including the laws pertaining to the Ministry of Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you now to look at item 7. It says: "With the conclusion, the government takes up position on issues which it has reviewed at a session, determines opinion on draft laws and other regulations, and on materials that were submitted to the assembly by other persons authorised to make proposals, decides on specific issues of internal organisation and relations within the government, determines the tasks of the ministries and bodies of the state administration, and the tasks of its services, and takes up positions on issues under its competence." Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, whether this is, again, a legal basis upon which the minister, including the minister of the interior, finds a legal basis for its act in the decision of the government?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After all of its sessions, the government reaches decisions which are distributed to all relevant ministries, which contain guidelines which ministries are obliged to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned in the pages of the transcript that were mentioned before, that the decisions of the president are obligatory for the minister. Why would the president's decision would be obligatory and why would they present a legal basis for the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is because of the fact that the president has certain authorisations according to the Law on Defence to issue certain orders, indications about the activities and actions of the police forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, I would kindly ask you to look now -- or I apologise. Before that, I would like to ask you whether this is also a basis that says that if authorised by the law, would then be a legal basis prescribed by the law, that the minister is able to bring a decision and order or another act foreseen in Article 55 of the Law on Civil Service?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, could the Law on Internal Affairs also give a direct authorisation to the minister? And if yes, would then the minister have the duty to enforce or apply that authorisation that is foreseen by the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Law on Internal Affairs has provisions which state that the minister is obliged to undertake certain measures which, in turn, he is obliged to carry through.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you now to look after tab 7 in the first binder and see Prosecutor's Exhibit P86, and Article 30 of this law. Article 30 reads: "In order to prevent committing criminal offences, finding and apprehending perpetrators of criminal offences as well as finding and securing evidence and traces of criminal offences, the authorised officials can close the entrances into a certain area or building and prevent somebody from leaving that area or building without permission. These measures will continue until the completion of the official activities." The paragraph 2 reads: "The minister or a person authorised by him can order undertaking the measures referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article." Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, with regards to Article 55 that you mentioned several times, that the minister can order, can issue order if authorised for this by the law, would this would be one of the examples that you were referring to or is this one example that corroborates your evidence before this Court?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is one example which we spoke about in correlation with Article 55 with the Law on Organisation and Work of State Administration Bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you now to look after tab 20 in this binder. Order issued on 6th of August, 2001. That is Exhibit P275. And as we can see, in the preamble that you discussed earlier as being the legal basis for passing of acts, the following is written: "Based on Article 55, paragraph 1 of the Law on Organisation and Work of State Administration Bodies, Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia 58 of the year 2000. Item 2 of the decision of the government of the Republic of Macedonia to establish a unit for special purposes. Confidential number 98/1, dated 12 June 2001. And part 1, item 1 and 2 of the decision of the president of the Republic of Macedonia to establish a temporary unit for combat against terrorism of classification A, D. T., Number 07-54 of 15 June 2001, the minister of the internal affairs brought the following order, to appoint the units of the Ministry of Internal Affairs that will become part of the temporary joint unit for combat against terrorism." Tell me, once again, when you were clarifying the matters to my learned friend, that the minister can issue an order if authorised for that by the law, was this decision and invoking the legal basis for it a corroboration for your answers given before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is so. This is another confirmation that the orders which the minister passes must be in accordance with Article 55 and the decisions of the government and the president of the Republic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, do you remember that during your yesterday's testimony you were shown a document that speaks about the preparations for the exhumation in Neprosteno. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you now to look at this document. This is after tab 44 in the second binder, and this is Exhibit 1D211. I would kindly ask you now to look at page 4, N000-0641, N000-0644, which begins: "President Trajkovski ..." We didn't have the English text here so I don't know the page number and I apologise to the registry for this. So on page 4 in Macedonian version, the paragraph starts: "President Trajkovski was agitated and spoke about the previous meeting with Mr. Jennes." Paragraph further below in the English version. Ms. Dorevska, you conclude that the minister was present in this meeting and this can be seen from this document. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, pursuant to the systemic Law on Organisation and Work of the State Administration, who represents the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would the same apply to the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if outside of a body of internal affairs if there are several persons attending a meeting with other ministries and with the foreigners, who would be the person representing the ministry at that moment?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister of the interior, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And whom would then the participants in the meetings, though even if president were one of those participants, whom would they address and why?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the minister of the interior, of course, because he is the one representing the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were then read the text that follows in the second paragraph after the one that I started reading out. And that is the paragraph which reads: "He told Mr. Boskoski, Mr. Minister, sir, we will immediately give all authorisation to the police. And he added, I am the president of this country," and that's it. Tell me, please, who gives the order here, is it the minister or the president?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the president of the state.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is the minister's [as interpreted] order a legal basis upon which a minister can act?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. The minister has the duty to act upon what the president has requested of him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown Exhibit 1D212.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's an error in the transcript. I'm not sure if I misspoke or if it's the interpretation. Line 11, it says: Is the minister's order a legal basis upon which a minister can act. What at least I wanted to say was whether the president's order is a legal basis upon which a minister can act.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I must say I thought you had said president.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, this is an investigator's note of the meeting which followed the meeting at which you spoke -- about which you spoke to my learned friend. Can we show page N000-0650.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very top of this document, this is a document in the English version. There is no Macedonian translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is no Macedonian version. That's why I'll read out to you the paragraph that I wish to draw your attention to and you will receive the interpretation in Macedonian. Paragraph 1 of the document states: "[In English] Mr. Boskoski said that he agreed with what was said, in principle, but he stated that he still had in mind the instructions of the president. It was not possible for him to decide." [Interpretation] Ms. Dorevska, does this note made by the OTP investigator Mr. Tucker confirm your testimony whereby Minister Boskoski had to act in accordance with the president's order?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it confirms that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Dorevska, do you recall being asked whether the minister's order to withdraw the police forces from the village of Aracinovo would constitute his operative powers - and I'm paraphrasing - and you answered that most probably this was a strategic decision or a government decision. Do you recall discussing this with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Petre Stojanovski testified before this Chamber and at page 9118 of the transcript, he stated as follows: "[In English] For clarification, immediately in the days before actually the Ministry of Interior took action to seize control over the village of Aracinovo and had clashes with the terrorists who were located there at that time. When the clashes started, an order was issued. I believe that it was an order issued by the president, the late president of the state, and probably pressured by the international public. The action was stopped and we were forced to provide a corridor for to allow the terrorists to be taken out of the village, having their complete armament with them." [Interpretation] Madam Dorevska, in view of this witness's testimony before this Tribunal, if the president ordered that the police force be stopped and that they withdraw, was this within the competence of the president, i.e., to order the engagement or the disengagement of the police forces?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally. This is what I said before, with regards to the provisions of the Law on Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The ministry and the relevant bodies within the ministry would have to act in accordance with the president's order, who, under the constitution and the law, is authorised to act this way?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would that be the minister's decision or the president's decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the president's decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you the provisions of Article 6, paragraph 2 of the Law on the Interior. Let us look at this again. You will find it at tab -- or, rather, behind tab 7. That's P86, Exhibit P86. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 6, which you discussed with the Prosecutor -- or, rather, you answered her questions and suggestions. It says: "The officers of the ministry have the duty to follow the orders of the minister and officially authorised by him with regards to performing the functions of the ministry unless the performance of these orders would consider the crime." Do you remember having discussed this and having stated that this is an obligation for the employee of the ministry, but does not pertain to the minister. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, you also talked about when it was that the minister could issue an order. Since we discussed previously your repeatedly stated position whereby the minister can issue orders which -- for which he has basis in the law, when you look at this decision did the minister of the interior know when under the law an authorised body gives him the authority to issue orders?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this provision of Article 6?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Article 6 deals with the obligations of the employees, as you said. However, in connection with this particular Article, you spoke with the Prosecutor about whether the minister is able to issue orders. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You reiterated that this was the case only that he could issue orders only where authorised by the law to do so?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago we looked at several orders and decisions authorising the minister -- for which, rather, the minister was authorised to issue them either by the Law on the Interior or by other legislation. When you testified about this, is it your understanding of this provision that the minister can issue orders where he is authorised to do so under the law and does this not confirm that Article 6, paragraph 1, refers only to employees and not the minister himself?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think these questions that are quite leading in nature and perhaps on issues of this nature. I would ask that my learned friend not lead so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sure Ms. Residovic will take notice of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember having been shown the document by Goran Zdravkovski. You'll find this behind tab 9 in the first binder, i.e., Exhibit 1D44. Do you also remember discussing this document with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall this, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, answering the questions put to you, you said that this was an original authorisation given to the then minister whereby he could order the engagement of the unit Tiger, and that in view of his original authority, he could delegate this authority to other persons. Do you recall answering questions to that effect?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you also recall stating at that time that in view of his original authority, it was not important or it didn't make any difference whether he delegated this authority orally or in writing or whether he delegated them to one person or several persons?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, when the Tigar Unit passed from the responsibility, inherent responsibility of the minister to the structure of the police department, did the minister after that retain the powers he had at the time when this document was written?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not! That would no longer be a case of his inherent responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown a telegram sent to Kocani finances sector, and you'll find it behind tab 37 of the second binder, which is Exhibit P468. Whilst explaining your understanding of the telegram at one point you said that you were able to notice one other thing which was that the telegram was addressed to the finances sector, which was directly attached to the minister. In other words, it was within the public security branch. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that in such a situation, the head of the bureau for public security would not be able to give instructions to a body which did not fall within his remit under the law, but, rather, within the remit of the minister. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the document behind tab 5, which is 1D107. Let's look at the page which has a diagram. We're referring to the document behind tab 5 -- or, rather, tab B. This might be 1D65, but nevertheless, they form part of a single document, 1D107. Since we'll be discussing the diagram only, let's look at 1D2342. The page I'm interested in is 1D242. It's the page before that one. That's one. Ms. Dorevska, please indicate where the finance sector is, the one you referred to a moment ago, as being directly attached to the minister.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. This is among the organisational units that are on the right-hand side and that are functionally linked to the minister of interior, so it is somewhere in the fifth box which says sector for finance and other joint matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Dorevska, please tell me where the department for international cooperation is, under whose jurisdiction does it fall?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, under the competence of the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember being shown a document from the meeting between Minister Boskoski and NATO representatives. That's the document behind table 25, which is 1D184, Exhibit 1D184. My learned friend asked you some questions about check-points and about how allegedly the minister assigned different individuals to different check-points, and do you recall discussing this?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, tell me this: When representatives of the ministry hold meetings with members of the international community, international organisations, who represents the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course minister of the interior, as his legal authorisations provide.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The relations with NATO and with ambassadors of other countries would fall under which part of the affairs of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document itself indicates it is written who has prepared it, it is in the area of international cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the -- according to the diagram we saw, this would fall under the competence of the minister. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to page 2 which is 1D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel please repeat the number of the page. It was too fast for the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the Macedonian version, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Here, the minister discussing the international cooperation with NATO, speaks of the disinformation that has been circulated around concerning the police force. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the minister were to suggest that an international organisation become involved in certain activities of the ministry, would that fall within his competence as the minister vis-a-vis the police and the police forces or does this form part of his international duties and powers?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, this is part of his international obligations and powers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know when we are having a break. Normally when we are working in the afternoon, I should be guided by you. Should I go on for another five minutes or shall we have the break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. I went on ten minutes late, thinking it would interrupt your line of questioning. But we'll break now and resume at ten past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Dorevska, do you recall my learned friend asking you on several occasions whether the heads of bodies within the ministry were independent in implementing the law. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Today you were again shown the amendment to the Law on the Interior from 2003, and you stated today that they had been independent or autonomous in their work previously because this had been regulated in the legislation governing state administration and they had to act accordingly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor put to you repeatedly that in the implementation of the law, the last say would be -- would -- had by the minister in terms of the competencies of the head of the bureau for public security. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We had occasion to see several orders and decisions issued by the minister, and in the preamble, as the legal authority, it was always Article 55 that was quoted of the Law on the Interior in implementing that legislation?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since that same law provided for the two bodies within the ministry, namely the bureau of public security and the directorate for security and counter-intelligence, does the fact that Article 55 was applicable confirm your evidence that the law had to be applied directly?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm objecting to the leading nature of these question, Your Honour. I think they are obviously on important matters and it's gone on for a while now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will move on, Your Honour. It does not matter, since the witness testified to that on several occasions. Can the witness be shown 65 ter 1D382. 65 ter 1D382.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, as you can see, this is the statement given by Fatmir Etemi to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY. Does the name Fatmir Etemi ring any bells?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise it as a name, but it doesn't mean much to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 3, where it states current occupation, it says that is he a member of the parliament. Does this indicate what his position was, that he was in fact a member of the parliament?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here it is stated that he was a member of the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to page N000-0031. That's 1D3581, if that's easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please focus on the following. I will read out part of the paragraph which starts with: "Two or three days ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in its English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And for that reason I will read this out to you, the first and the last sentences: "[In English] Two or three days after the attack, I had a meeting with the minister of interior, Ljube Boskoski, the deputy minister of the interior, Refet Elmazi and Goran Mitevski, the head of the public security." [Interpretation] The last sentence says: "[In English] Boskoski told Mitevski to release all the detainees except three of them, but Mitevski said that he could not do it since 25 of them were shown positive at the paraffin test." [Interpretation] Ms. Dorevska, is this reaction on the part of Mr. Mitevski, in the presence of the minister and deputy minister, indicative of his independent acting in implementing the law and in exercising the authorities within his remit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I say, Ms. Residovic, your question assumes that these facts are established. They are merely recorded here in a statement which is not an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pardon? Yes, Your Honour. I do understand that this is not evidence. I'm merely asking whether this statement confirms what the witness stated, whether this serves to corroborate or merely shows that it's consistent with her testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I think what you'll have to do is put the question on the conditional basis that if this last sentence were correct, would it show ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Dorevska, with the assistance of the Presiding Judge, I will put the question to you in the proper form. If the statement given by this witness to the ICTY investigator that Mr. Mitevski did not accept this suggestion by the minister for the release of certain individuals because the facts that he had at his disposal were irrelevant to him, if this statement were true would it confirm that the head of the public security bureau was performing his duties independently?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I think this is in accordance with my testimony in the course of yesterday that when police matters are concerned that the director of the public security is independent in their execution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify, Your Honour, the way in which my learned friend phrased her question that Mitevski did not accept the direction or the release by Minister Boskoski isn't precisely the way that it is stated in the statement. And, of course, it was put in a very leading form and the witness has already answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: All correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Dorevska, do you recall my learned friend showing to you the decision to set up the staff for the operative action of Ramno, issued by Minister Dosta Dimovska. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to tab 86 of the second binder and look at Exhibit 1D112. 86. Before we discuss this decision, tell me this: You also discussed with my learned friend the fact that the minister can vary or adopt a decision issued by the previous minister. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You accepted this statement as true. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What are the possible reasons for a minister to issue an order varying an earlier decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There can be many such reasons. The staff could change, there could be reassignment of people who are part of this decision to other workplaces, organisational changes. Many other changes as a result of which he can do this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Madam Dorevska, when a commission is being set up, or a staff, how does this come about? Is there a uniform procedure for the setting up of such bodies? Can you please tell us what your experience in that regard is, since in your sector you often-times drafted such decisions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister determines the staff involved and this is most often according to the work posts of certain employees in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Madam Dorevska, on some occasions is it important for the composition of a commission to determine which body or organ is represented on that particular commission?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in some situations where a commission or some other body, a staff is being set up, is it important for such a body to comprise representatives of important bodies of the ministry, or, in other words, is it important to have the sector for legal affairs, the state security sector represented there and so on?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand the question now. Of course it is important depending on the area which this decision deals with. Depending on this will be -- will determine the persons who are part of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If it so happens that at the head of this body, or, rather, that the person heading this body is replaced by someone else, and therefore certain body of the ministry is not represented anymore, what happens next?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case, that part of the decision is changed, and that person, which had until then, occupied that workplace is occupied -- is replaced with the person who now takes that workplace.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at 1D112. Under item 1, we have Zvonko Kasirski, head of the bureau of -- for public security. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under item 2, we have the acting head of the office for security and counter-intelligence. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Next we have the under-secretary of -- for the police who is a police general. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Next we have the deputy under-secretary of the police and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so. All relevant structures in the bureau for public security, including the director of the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, director of security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the person heading some of these important departments of the ministry would be replaced, what would happen with the decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If decision still needs to remain in place, then of course this will be changed. The person who will have a new contract will include the person who will have a new contract for that work post.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel and the witness please break between question and answer because the interpreters have difficulties to follow. And could Madam Residovic repeat the relevant numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Behind tab 22, Exhibit P381 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you go on, Ms. Residovic, the interpreters missed some of the last answer and are asking if it can repeated. They would like, in particular, the witness to repeat the numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Rather, Madam Residovic. The witness's answer was fully interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I was looking in the wrong direction. It's what you were saying, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it was merely numbers of the different exhibits. Behind tab 22, Exhibit P381.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Dorevska, under item 1, which is the body that is represented here in this modified decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this is the director of the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the post under number 2?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Director of the bureau for security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which body is under number 3?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the head of the department of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under number 4?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant head of the department for police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And so on and so forth. Madam Dorevska, are these organs completely identical to those contained in the decision dated 7 March 2001 issued by Minister Dosta Dimovska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. These are the same bodies in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what led to the issuing of the second decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A change in the person who were on those work posts, the persons who headed the bureau for public security and the bureau for security and counter-intelligence have changed, as well as the persons represented in some of the other bodies listed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did something happen in May of 2001, that would lead to such a considerable change in the persons holding significant positions of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of May 2001, a broad coalition government was established, and certain work posts fell under a different political option.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To what extent does that constitute a reason, based on which a minister should modify or vary a decision that was adopted earlier?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the minister must change the decision because those persons on those posts were different.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As for this decision, this staff or a commission, as you put it, the important matter is that all these bodies are represented in it, is it not?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it is important, because we're talking about the setting up of an operative headquarters and operative activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Madam Dorevska, do you recall my learned friend suggesting to you on Friday that Goran Mitevski had been appointed head of public security two days after Minister Boskoski had been elected minister? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Dorevska, do you know Goran Mitevski?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: How long had Goran Mitevski been working in the police before he was appointed to that duty?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mitevski has been employed in the ministry a few years before my arrival, which means 14, 15 years of continual employment to the moment of his appointment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what's his profession?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mitevski has graduated from the faculty of security studies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That means that also he is a police officer by his educational background. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, is he a professional and a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the appointment to the office of the director of bureau for public security, as far as you know, considering that you occupied those posts, did Goran Mitevski perform any other senior duties, occupy a senior managerial position?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he was working in the bureau for security and counter-intelligence as head of sector. Then he was the acting head, director of the bureau for security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If some post of appointed official is vacated for some reason because of a death or transfer to another office, resignation, et cetera, how could this post be populated until a new office holder is appointed?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the way as it was done with Mr. Goran Mitevski. The minister of interior can, with a temporary act, place a person to carry out a function until the permanent appointment of that person on that post.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you recall who was the minister during the time when Goran Mitevski was appointed acting head of another body within the ministry, that was the bureau for security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the period of the December 2000, when the minister was Ms. Dosta Dimovska.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with my apologies for having no translation because we received this document two days ago and we were not able to translate it, I would kindly ask that the witness is shown 65 ter 1D1280. I would read the Macedonian text and ask that it is interpreted so that the Chamber and the others could follow the document because I wish to ask questions of the witness with regards to that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, you have in front of you the document. You see in-- in the upper corner that we received this document by fax on the 17th of February. If we -- no, we need to show the upper part of the document, yes. Here, you see it that the document was received by the Defence on the 17th of February. And now it reads: "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior, number 232-40929/1, 5 December 2000, Skopje." And it reads: "On the basis of Article 57, paragraph 1 of the Law on Organisation and Operation of the Bodies of State Administration, Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia, number 58 of year 2000, and Article 31, paragraph 1, of the collective agreement of the Ministry of the Interior, Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia, number 8 of year 1998, I enact the decision, Goran Mitevski, head of the bureau for counter-intelligence, in the directorate for security and counter-intelligence, within the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia, is temporarily tasked in addition to the jobs and tasks at the post of head of the bureau for counter-intelligence within the DBK, with the performance of the activities and tasks within the remit of the post of the director of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence within the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia as of 5th of December, 2000." "This term of office will be valid until a director of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence within the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia is appointed by the government of the Republic of Macedonia. Rationale, because of the dismissal of the director of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence within the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia, and for the best interest of more efficient performance of the functions of the ministry and particularly because of the importance of the duties entailed in the aforementioned post, the decision was made as written above. The employee has the right to appeal this decision, to the second instance committee in the area of employment and labour within the government of the Republic of Macedonia, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the decision, through the minister of internal affairs. A copy of this decision is served to the appointed person, the directorate of finance and other common affairs and the bureau for legal and personnel affairs. Signed Minister Dosta Dimovska." Are you aware of this decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision prepared in this sector at that time, bureau for legal affairs and personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, considering that -- or, rather, tell me first whether the director for state security or the acting director of the bureau for public security is a high professional office in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this office any less important or is it rather in the same rank as the office of the director of the bureau for public security?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're on the same level. Two bodies within the framework of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, why was Goran Mitevski appointed to the bureau for public security and not to the state security? Do you know the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, as I said previously, this was the period of May 2001, when the broad coalition government was set up and the work post of director of the direction for security and counter-intelligence fell under a different political option, and then Mr. Zoran Verusevski was appointed as its director. I believe this was the reason why Mr. Goran Mitevski was appointed, therefore, the director of public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the suggestion put by my learned friend, that Goran Mitevski came to this office since he was nominated by the Minister Boskoski and that he was, in a way, linked, if I may say so, to the Minister Boskoski, is there any basis for this assertion in your -- in as far as you know, Mr. Goran Mitevski and the duties that he performed at the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course this is not important in this context. As I said, this is a person who is a professional, who has a long work and employment experience behind him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have concluded my cross-examination of this witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. You will be pleased to know, Ms. Dorevska, that that completes the questions for you. We would like to thank you for your attendance here and your patient assistance and you may, of course, now return to your normal activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I wish you further success in your work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The court officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would suggest -- or, rather, I would seek to tender as Defence exhibit from this re-direct examination, 65 ter 1278, that is the application of Zoran Krstevski to the Macedonian Radio and Television for the termination of his employment there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D307, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, Your Honours, I seek to tender document 65 ter 1D1280, and we would additionally submit a translation as soon as it is finished. That is the decision of Minister Dosta Dimovska appointing Goran Mitevski as acting director of the UBK. We would seek to tender this document as well in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D308, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I note the time, and considering the time we have available, I ask that I do not start the examination of the expert witness because I have just few minutes to spend with her. But I would like to ask you if, with your permission, to spend this time adding to our 65 ter list additional evidence so that we do not take up Court's time with this tomorrow. That is the C.V. of Professor Slagjana Taseva, Ph.D. That is 65 ter 1D1277. Then 65 ter 1D1279; that is a report produced by Slagjana Taseva, Ph.D. And 65 ter 1D1276; that is an excerpt from the glossary that CLSS submitted to the Defence and which we will probably use during the examination of Professor Taseva.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If there is no objection, yes, those -- that will be allowed, Ms. Residovic. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. Except for my request that we start the examination of the witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we will adjourn now, Ms. Residovic, to resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I just raise a very brief procedural matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I have been instructed by our court officer and by my case manager to put on the record that there will be three additional translations linked to Exhibit P00402 on e-court, and the document identification numbers are N000-9692, N000-9696 and N000-9700. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of February, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.49 p.m.,
